messages:
incident-bot: Paging: p99 latency breach detected for service `streaming-prod` (5m p99 = 2.42s, SLO=1.2s). Streaming stalls increased, clients reporting stalls/seek timeouts. Possible GPU node degradation in cluster-us-west-2. Runbook: https://rwd.infra/runbooks/streaming-latency

jen (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it. @kevin can you pull GPU node health and ECC logs? I'll start mitigation steps from runbook (route fallback + scale up pools).

kevin (eng-sre): grabbing node list now. Seeing elevated correctable ECC on gpu-node-12 and 17. Running quick `dmesg | tail -n 80` to confirm.

maria (infra): FYI cooling telemetry for that rack shows spikes starting ~10:23 UTC, fan duty climbed to 100% briefly. Could be thermal.

kevin (eng-sre): paste: ```
Mar 15 10:26:42 gpu-node-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=3210, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 10:26:42 gpu-node-12 kernel: Correctable ECC error on GPU 0: 12 count(s)
Mar 15 10:26:45 gpu-node-12 kernel: thermal_alert: GPU 0 throttle engaged
```

jen (oncall): thanks. That lines up with increase in streaming tail latency. @lee any model-level indicators? KV cache pressure, long prefix hops?

lee (ml-infra): model telemetry shows spike in KV cache misses for session tokens, and sequence lengths unchanged. Streaming stalls correlated with sessions pinned to gpu-node-12. When node stalls, requests get queued and p99 spikes. We're seeing stall timeouts at 15-20s in the streaming layer.

sam (support): support reports 12 incidents in last 20m, a couple customers complaining about audio/video stalls in the product integration. No 5xxs logged, just slow streaming and some session resets.

jen (oncall): mitigation plan (live): 1) remove gpu-node-12 and 17 from routing (mark draining) 2) enable fallback routing to `streaming-prod-fallback` model variant 3) temporary autoscale +2 nodes to absorb load 4) notify support and customers. I'll execute in that order.

kevin (eng-sre): draining nodes now: ```
$ rwctl node drain gpu-node-12 --reason "ECC/thermal spike"
node gpu-node-12: set to DRAINING
$ rwctl node drain gpu-node-17 --reason "ECC/thermal spike"
node gpu-node-17: set to DRAINING
```

jen (oncall): routing change command: ```
$ rwctl route set --service streaming-prod --fallback-model streaming-small-8b --priority 10
route updated, new fallback in place
```

alert-bot: Routing change applied for `streaming-prod`: fallback -> `streaming-small-8b`. Telemetry will take ~1m to reflect.

maria (infra): kicked a cooling job to increase airflow, but if thermal is persistent we'll replace the node. Ops ticket created: OPS-4521.

kevin (eng-sre): eviction attempt shows one slot failing to re-schedule because some pods pinned to the node had long-lived TCP connections. Forcing session migration now.

lee (ml-infra): session migration script run: ```
$ scripts/migrate-sessions --from gpu-node-12 --to random-healthy
migrated 840 sessions, avg migration time 210ms
```

jen (oncall): good. after fallback and drain, 5m p99 dropped to 1.05s. Streaming stalls reduced but not gone (still occasional 2-3s spikes). Marking escalation as partial mitigated.

sam (support): sending status to affected customers: "We're mitigating increased latency by routing traffic to fallback models and draining a hardware node. Expect improvements within minutes. We'll follow up after full validation." :thumbsup:

kevin (eng-sre): deeper log sample from gpu-node-12 NVML: ```
GPU 0: correctable ECC count: 184 -> 217 in 12m
GPU 0: thermal_throttle_count: 6 in 12m
syslog: repeated Xid 79 followed by driver reset attempts
```

lee (ml-infra): note: fallback model has slightly higher perplexity on some prompts, but tradeoff acceptable for latency SLO. We'll flag a quality regression alert for post-incident eval.

jen (oncall): @maria can you coordinate hardware replacement for gpu-node-12 if ECC keeps rising? Also rough ETA to have node back without eviction?

maria (infra): I can RMA the board, ETA parts 4-6 hours. If we need hot-swap immediate, can move workloads permanently off node and reprovision a new VM with spare GPU, ~45-60m.

alert-bot: Observability: p95=0.58s, p99=1.02s (down from 2.42s), stream timeout rate reduced from 0.9% -> 0.12% after routing change.

sam (support): customers updated. one enterprise customer asked for SLA credit guidance, forwarding to account team.

kevin (eng-sre): initiated a background scan for any other nodes showing similar ECC ramp: running `nvtool cluster-ecc-scan --window 15m` now.

lee (ml-infra): adding a temporary rule to smart router so that any session pinned to a node with >50 correctable ECC in 15m is proactively migrated. ```
$ rwctl router scale-policy set --service streaming-prod --ecc-threshold 50 --action migrate
```

jen (oncall): nice. That should reduce tail risk. I'll start handoff to the next on-call in 30m. Current status: mitigations executed, partial mitigation confirmed, hardware RMA opened, customer comms done. Postmortem + Q-profile should be scheduled.

kevin (eng-sre): cluster scan shows two more nodes with small upticks but below threshold: gpu-node-21 (22 ECC), gpu-node-8 (30 ECC). We'll keep them monitored.

maria (infra): opened ops-run: "investigate cooling loop for rack 7" and scheduled swap for gpu-node-12 if ECC > 250 or thermal persists.

jen (oncall): handing off to @kevin for next 2 hours. Please maintain watch and follow RMA/replace plan. If p99 creeps above 1.2s again, escalate to eng-sre on-call and paging.

kevin (eng-sre): taking over. I'll keep thread updated. Thanks all.

sam (support): closing initial customer broadcast ticket, will reopen if new reports come in.

alert-bot: Incident note: mitigation applied at 10:42 UTC (drain + fallback). Monitoring will auto-close if p99 < 1.2s for 30m.

jen (oncall): quick post-incident notes: likely root cause = thermal-induced ECC increases leading to intermittent GPU driver resets, causing streaming stalls and p99 spikes. Immediate fix = drain & fallback. Longer term: automated node migration on ECC ramp + improved cooling/replace flaky cards.

kevin (eng-sre): logging for postmortem: saved NVML dumps and dmesg from affected nodes to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/9951122334/

maria (infra): OPS-4521 updated with swap plan and estimated SLA impact for affected customers.

jen (oncall): if nobody objects, I'll mark this as "partial mitigated" and tag for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

lee (ml-infra): +1. I'll create an eval run comparing pre/post fallback output quality and attach to the postmortem.

sam (support): +1, keeping channel on watch for 1h then closing.

kevin (eng-sre): p99 currently stable at 0.98s for last 10m. Leaving active-watch.

alert-bot: last_message: status updated to WATCH.
